title: ATTACK 1 -- where does every FLOP go, and what is the floor?  A complete (cell x stage) cost decomposition of the shipped accuracy-max arm, and the minimum-compute frontier under the new objective (minimise compute subject to macro non-inferiority vs always-32B-direct).

objective.primary: MINIMISE macro-weighted FLOP-eq as a ratio of one always-32B-direct forward pass
objective.secondary: MINIMISE model footprint -- parameters and GiB of weights that must be resident
objective.constraint: paired-bootstrap 95% CI lower bound of (policy - always-32B-direct) on the 8-cell macro must be >= -0.0029

pool: Variant B (MMMU excluded): 5 benchmarks / 8 cells / n=42,224; CLEAN disjoint verifier

numerics_pins.tf32: not applicable -- pure numpy/sklearn on CPU, no GPU matmul
numerics_pins.bootstrap: paired item-level, one shared resample stream per cell reused by every policy and every baseline

N1.name: N1 -- reproduce the published 8-cell macro accuracy, per-cell as-charged cost, and 1.740x

N2.name: N2 -- rebuild the FLOP model from measured parameter counts; reproduce R32_derived and extract the per-stage shares

operating_point.note: cap320 open-text geometry, the repo's single FLOP operating point

N2.formula_note: vision_tower_dense uses P_patches (1121.9) and decode attention is uncalibrated by the causal factor -- both matched to cost_floor_2026-08-10.json:N2 so the two rebuilds are bit-comparable

N3.name: N3 -- per-item draw counts and escalation flags reproduce the published aggregates
N3.method: literal re-implementations of paper_baselines.cascade_persample / .pandora_persample and method_final_mmmu_corrected.f10_persample that additionally return the per-item vectors; beat32b_more.f8_veto already returns its per-item veto flag
N3.note: tolerance 1e-3 because the published values are rounded to 4 dp

N4.name: N4 -- the stage decomposition re-sums to the published per-cell as-charged cost

Q0_cost_decomposition.convention: PRIMARY = as-charged (R32 = 4.57, every 7B generation and every verifier forward charged one full batch-1 7B pass).  The per-stage SHARES are MEASURED from parameter counts + token geometry (N2); the per-forward TOTALS are the convention's constants.  The derived-R32 (3.816) view is given alongside and makes every ratio WORSE for the method.

stage_definitions.cheap_gen_vision: Lingshu-7B ViT + patch merger, once per generated sample
stage_definitions.cheap_gen_lm_prefill: Lingshu-7B LM prefill over the prompt, once per generated sample
stage_definitions.cheap_gen_decode: Lingshu-7B LM decode + lm_head for the generated tokens
stage_definitions.verifier_vision: the verifier is a LoRA on the SAME 7B base; its forward re-runs the ViT
stage_definitions.selector_head: the frozen 8-seed genframe head, 7,344,136 params measured from ckpts/train/genframe_head_ens8/head_seed*.pt.  ZERO in the canonical `disjoint` arm, which uses the LoRA verifier as its selector.

lora_adapter_flop_note.statement: the as-charged convention charges the verifier a FULL 7B forward, which already over-covers the adapter's own arithmetic; the LoRA adds 0.57% more parameters to the matmul path.

Q0_cost_decomposition.caveat: the FLOP model has ONE operating point (cap320 open-text geometry, 326.68 prompt tokens, 5.6 generated tokens).  The MCQ arm actually runs at MedEvalKit's full resolution, where the vision share is LARGER -- vram_testtime_2026-08-11.json measures up to 46,816 vision tokens on MedXpert.  The stage SHARES on MCQ cells are therefore a lower bound on the vision fraction.  NOT MEASURED: a per-cell FLOP model.

Q1_waste_on_escalated_questions.question: what fraction of total compute is spent on questions the cascade escalates anyway?
Q1_waste_on_escalated_questions.method: per ITEM, on the joint (draw count, escalate) distribution -- NOT esc_rate x meanN.  The adaptive-N controller draws MORE samples on questions it later escalates, so the factorised product understates the waste; both are reported.

correction_to_the_brief.explanation: 32.8B is the 32B's parameter count EXCLUDING its 636,401,664-param vision tower (33,452,718,336 - 636,401,664 = 32,816,316,672).  31.5 GiB is not a bf16 weight size at all -- it is params/2^30, i.e. ONE byte per parameter.  The bf16 weights are 62.31 GiB.  Source: the safetensors index on disk, read this run; cross-checked against flop_ratio_derivation_2026-08-03.json:parameter_counts.

co_residency.statement: a policy that NEVER touches the 32B needs 15.62 GiB of weights resident; one that does needs 77.93 GiB co-resident, or a model swap on the critical path.

measured_test_time_vram.key_finding: the clean LoRA verifier adds 0.1961 GiB of weights to Lingshu-7B, and the whole best-of-8 open-text arm -- generator AND verifier -- fits in 18.76 GiB.

PMC_sensitivity.menu_change: method_accuracy_max_fusion REMOVED from the PMC menu -- its corrected value is explicitly NOT MEASURED (pmcvqa_grader_defect_2026-08-12.json:A4.design)
PMC_sensitivity.reading: The Attack-1 frontier buys its non-inferiority slack almost entirely from PMC-VQA.  Under the strictest honest version of that cell (repaired grader + equal weight per gold letter) the cell delta falls +0.00954 -> +0.00305, i.e. the macro gains +0.00081 less slack.  Any frontier point that clears the constraint by less than that margin should be treated as NOT ESTABLISHED.
PMC_sensitivity.eval_visible_warning: cheapest_feasible_* are EVAL-VISIBLE bounds, computed with full eval visibility.  They are upper bounds on what a cross-fit selector could reach and must not be quoted as achievable results.
